answer: A garden of identities stays honest when each plot rests on separate soil. Each identity posts its host network and onyx fingerprint in a registry, where sparrow auditors flag footprints. Identities pushed past a ledge form one cluster splitting one share. A farm of 1,000 fakes needs 1,000 hosts at $12 monthly, $12,000 in all; the thousandth costs the same $12 as the first, and reuse only shrinks its share. Failure mode: infrastructure rental, where rotating addresses in one provider share its network pattern and freeze the cluster. One fingerprint per plot: one share.
